title: Read your activity
description: Short XRP Mobile tutorial: read your transaction history. Switch the wallet home from balances to activity, find any payment sent or received, and open its receipt: counterparty, network fee, date, status and the transaction hash you can check on a public XRP Ledger explorer. Also, what those tiny incoming amounts you never asked for are, and why you should ignore them.
lede: Did that payment actually go through? Every transaction your wallet has ever made or received is one tap away, with the receipt that settles the argument.

steps.caption: Balances, then history
steps.body: The wallet home has two tabs. Currencies is what you hold right now. Activity is how it got there.

steps.caption: Everything in and out
steps.body: Every payment, sent and received, newest first, with the amount in XRP and in your own currency. The tiny incoming amounts you do not recognise are spam: the XRP Ledger lets anyone send you a fraction of a cent, and some senders use it to advertise. Ignore them, and never follow a link one of them carries.

steps.caption: Open one for the receipt
steps.body: Tap any entry to open its receipt.

steps.caption: Fee, status and hash
steps.body: Who it went to, what the network charged, the date, and whether it completed. At the bottom, the transaction hash: that is the proof. Copy it, or open it in the explorer to see the same payment on the public ledger, from outside the app.

steps.caption: Back to your balances
steps.body: Back out and you are on your balances again. Nothing here is stored by us: the list is read from the XRP Ledger every time you open it.
